text: Sarvatra Samabuddhaya - under any circumstances, meditating, not meditating, walking, eating, working, can I keep my mind tranquil and not agitated? If this is possible, then we are leading a spiritual life. If this is not possible, whatever rituals you do, whatever yoga you practice, you may stand for two hours on your head and wave your legs in the sky, you are not leading a spiritual life.
author: Sri M

text: When happiness comes, don’t get too excited. And when pain comes, don’t get too depressed. To stay in this state at all times, is the meaning of the word Sthitaprajna, in the Gita.
author: Sri M

text: The morning one and the evening sandhya are very important times when we should remember our link and connection with the Supreme Being. If we do that, throughout the day whatever work we do, whatever joys we get, and whatever pains we experience, all these will be set in a proper order.
author: Sri M

text: I know people who have billions or more, but they are not happy. If we think that because somebody has a lot of money, that person is happy, we are labouring under a big illusion. There are people who have nothing and are happy. So, the happiness quotient does not depend on what you have and what you don't have. It is the blessing of the Supreme Being.
author: Sri M

text: Under all circumstances, keep your mind peaceful, quiet, tranquil. Because action that comes out of a tranquil mind is usually the right action. Action that comes out of an agitated mind cannot be proper action.
author: Sri M

text: We think that we are advancing, improving, when there is plenty, goodness and when there is happiness. It's pain and sorrow that makes us move forward. When that comes, don't try to run and say, take it off! It will be taken off if you say, take it off. But one would not have learned the lesson, why it is there, why has it come.
author: Sri M

text: The wise look for the good and don't care for the pleasant. Fools look for the pleasant and forget the good. They fall for the pleasant and forget what is good, because the good may not always be pleasant. Choose the good in preference to the pleasant.
author: Sri M

text: No sacrifice is a sacrifice if you are not giving what is closest to you, with a full heart. That's not a sacrifice.
author: Sri M

text: If you need to understand the essence of the teachings of this country, which is also universal, Lokah samastah sukhino bhavantu, you have to go to the Upanishads.
author: Sri M

text: Don’t unnecessarily complicate life with too many things. Speak the truth; More than speaking the truth, think the truth. That does not mean that when you speak the truth you have to be blunt. There are sweet ways of speaking the truth. You need not be brusque and then suffer because of that.
author: Sri M

text: According to Vedanta that feeling of being dependent on what is around you, the feeling that you are bound and that you have to get out of it, is part of the great illusion of the mind called the Maya.
author: Sri M

text: What is that one attains in the grihastha period which is different from the brahmacharya period? Once you are married you have one more person in your life; you cannot take independent and exclusive decisions. You learn to control your emotions, control your anger and to look at the other person’s point of view
author: Sri M

text: Freedom is our birthright. Our true self, the atman is free; it does not need to be freed from anything. It is free because it is complete, ‘purna’. ‘Purnamadah’ - That completeness is actually ‘you’ in your true essence.
author: Sri M

text: Remove all the conditions that are there and remain in that One essential state. This is the aim of the Vedantic teaching. One discovers that one is not this body nor the mind but the inner self, the atman which is free of all unhappiness and which by essential nature is Sat Chit Ananda, or true happiness.
author: Sri M

text: When you enter the meditation hall, leave your shoes outside along with your ego; don’t bring it in. Go inside like a new-born child who is free, you have no enemies, you don’t hate anybody, at least for the time being. This is easier said than done but it’s the easiest way to bring about a completely tranquil and deep meditative mind.
author: Sri M

text: Once all illusions are burnt to ashes, one arrives at supreme satisfaction, unlimited bliss and happiness. Therefore one has no other desire left. This happens when the Kundalini reaches the ajna chakra, which is the last but one step towards Moksha.
author: Sri M

text: Mantra is a technique and not the goal. When you feel you have entered a deep state and chanting the mantra also takes effort, Stop! But watch out, the mind is very tricky, it may be laziness which may be preventing you from chanting. So, examine carefully.
author: Sri M

text: Shivam cannot be touched without the activation of the Shakti. Without the havan kund, no homa can be done.
author: Sri M

text: Moving up and down the spine is Mukhya Prana, the Supreme energy. In yogic terms, it is the movement of the aspiration, thought, concentration and energy towards either the higher side or the lower side. When it goes down it leads to material wellbeing. When it goes up, it leads to Spiritual wellbeing.
author: Sri M

text: A spiritual teacher sometimes provides opportunities and situations, either deliberately or as they happen. He does not encourage people to run away from situations but to pause and remain. It is only when faced with a particular set of circumstances, one begins to realise for oneself where one stands.
author: Sri M

It is only when faced with a particular set of circumstances, one begins to realise for oneself where one stands.
author: Sri M

text: When you practice the techniques taught through the spiritual texts, you will come to a stage where your mind is no more limited to the brain but is multidimensional.
author: Sri M

text: When you practice the techniques taught through the spiritual texts, you will come to a stage where your mind is no more limited to the brain but is multidimensional.
author: Sri M

text: We have the most complex brain, better than any other animals therefore we tend to think that it is because of this that everything is functioning. Consciousness can be totally free of the brain and act on its own if required.
author: Sri M

text: Be a bhakta - devotee more than anything else because through bhakti all jnana - wisdom will dawn.
author: Sri M

text: When you have gone deep enough in your meditation, in your spiritual practice, you are not aware of the outside world in a state of deep trance, you are not even thinking of any idea what you should do or what you should not do, suddenly a thought will come into your mind. You may not even have thought about it and it's not even from your subconscious. It comes deep from within and then you know, yes, this is to be done, then it's your inner Guru speaking. It may not even be speaking in words. It may be suddenly that you realize, I know this.
author: Sri M

text: As you journey on the path, the more you desire, the more is your aspiration towards having a glimpse of the Supreme, then something very soft and nice grows in your heart. It's very fragrant. And when it grows, that is devotion.
author: Sri M

text: It is the function of the Outer Guru, a teacher, to bring about the development of the student so that he / she becomes more reliant on the Inner Guru than the Outer Guru. The Outer Guru can disappear, but the Inner does not. The Inner Guru is actually none other than the Supreme Being.
author: Sri M

text: The function of the Guru is to show a mirror to you. To clean the mirror and show it properly at the right angle so that you see yourself as you actually are, not what you want to be.
author: Sri M

text: When you say Guru, it means a teacher in all ways; could be a small child who teaches you innocence of childhood, it could be a philosophical teacher who teaches you the Upanishads, they are all Gurus.
author: Sri M
